cls: Topical haemostatic and antiseptic agent (iron-polyacrylate complex)

summary: Feracrylum is a topical haemostatic and antiseptic agent - an incomplete ferric/ferrous salt of partially hydrolysed polyacrylic acid (a high-molecular-weight iron-polyacrylate complex), supplied as a 1% solution (also gel and impregnated dressing). On contact with blood it complexes with serum proteins (chiefly albumin) to form a water-insoluble gel/film that acts as a mechanical barrier and arrests capillary oozing within minutes, and it has independent antimicrobial activity. It is used topically on minor wounds, abrasions, surgical/dental bleeding and leech bites, and as an antiseptic dressing. Because of its high molecular weight it is not systemically absorbed, so it has essentially no systemic toxicity, interactions, or organ-dose considerations. It is water-soluble and non-staining, allowing relatively atraumatic dressing changes. It is marketed in India and is not FDA-approved; its evidence base is limited to small studies and reviews.
indications: Topical control of capillary/minor bleeding and oozing (cuts, abrasions, minor burns, post-operative and dental extraction sites, leech bites)
Antiseptic management/dressing of wounds to reduce infection
Adjunct haemostasis in minor surgical and oral surgical procedures

admin: For external/topical use only - not for oral, intravenous or intramuscular use
Apply the 1% solution directly or on soaked gauze with light pressure to the bleeding site

Use as a sterile single-use product per the label
moa: On contact with blood, feracrylum complexes with serum proteins (notably albumin) to form a large, water-insoluble gel/film coagulum that acts as a mechanical barrier and stops capillary oozing within minutes; thrombin activation and fibrinogen-to-fibrin conversion are also described as contributing to clot formation. It additionally has antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and fungi, and is hygroscopic, maintaining a moist wound-healing environment.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to feracrylum or any component
Internal use (oral, intravenous or intramuscular) - external use only
relative: Use under medical advice in pregnancy/lactation (limited data)
monitor: Wound for local irritation or signs of infection

preg: As a topical agent with negligible systemic absorption (high molecular weight), systemic risk in pregnancy is expected to be minimal; however, formal safety data are lacking. Use under medical advice and inform the clinician if pregnant or planning pregnancy.
lact: Topical use with negligible systemic absorption is expected to pose minimal risk during breastfeeding, but formal data are limited - use under medical advice.
renal: Not applicable for topical use - the high-molecular-weight complex is not systemically absorbed; studies report no adverse effects on renal function.
hepatic: Not applicable for topical use - not systemically absorbed; studies report no adverse hepatic effects.

minor: One manufacturer insert advises caution with concurrent epsilon-aminocaproic acid (label caution, weakly substantiated)
interactions.diagnostics: No systemic laboratory effects; acts locally at the wound.

rare: Local burning/stinging sensation or transient irritation at the application site
emergency: Signs of a local hypersensitivity reaction (marked irritation, rash)

monitoring: Clinical assessment of haemostasis (oozing should stop within minutes)
